reply.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color Ally and Lesson pile that draws cards off bending triggers and grows lands into creatures. Appa and the other Aang flip-sides line up into an infinite combo with [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and either [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] producing infinite tokens and ETB triggers.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Chromatic Lantern]] toward casting [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Cast bending-themed Lesson spells to trigger draw from [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] and flip it.

Assemble [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] alongside [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite tokens.
Grow lands into creatures via earthbend effects like [[Earthbending Lesson]] and swing with Ally support from [[Katara, Water Tribe's Hope]].
Use airbend exile effects such as [[Airbending Lesson]] to rebuy permanents cheaply from exile.

keep.text: Early mana into [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] sets up the token engine.
A hand with ramp and a Lesson like [[Airbending Lesson]] keeps options open.

sendBack.text: A hand missing colored sources for five colors struggles to cast Lessons.
Too few lands to reach [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] by turn 4 is a liability.

tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] can airbend [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to exile and recast it cheaply, retriggering its enter effect.
[[Uncle Iroh]] reduces the cost of Lesson spells like [[Water Whip]], making the waterbend additional cost easier to pay.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends extra when you cast a Lesson, synergizing with [[Earthbending Lesson]].

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Draws cards off bending and flips into a payoff.
Airbends permanents and makes tokens from exile casts.
Airbends a permanent on entry, enables the loop.

keyCards.card: Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury
keyCards.job: Flash airbend body that transforms into an attacker.
Accelerates mana toward the commander.
Earthbends lands into creatures on spellcasting.
Flash flier that draws cards off library searches.

assessment.line: The deck leans on enchantments like [[Sanctum of Calm Waters]] with no answer to opposing artifacts or enchantments.
Only 2 interaction cards, with 1 at instant speed, leaves little to stop a fast threat like an opposing combo piece.
Without [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] on board the card draw engine and the infinite line both stall.
Removing [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] before its enter trigger resolves breaks the infinite token loop.
Five colors demand heavy fixing, and a slow draw of basics can strand Lesson spells like [[Water Whip]] uncastable.

reply.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifact counters deck that taps artifacts and creatures to pile up charge and +1/+1 counters, then proliferates repeatedly to snowball value and set up one of several combos such as [[Basalt Monolith]] plus [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana or [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.

strategy.text: Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 to start proliferating whenever it taps.
Ramp with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to accelerate into the midgame.
Grow counters with cards like [[Contagion Engine]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], then proliferate to multiply them.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana when possible.
Close the game with [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.

keep.text: Holding [[Sol Ring]] alongside an early play keeps the mana curve on track.
A hand with [[Pemmin's Aura]] and a creature to enchant sets up the engine early.

sendBack.text: All one color with no path to the Jeskai mana base is too risky.
No ramp pieces among 12 in the deck means a slow, clunky start.

tips.text: Use [[Pemmin's Aura]] to untap [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] repeatedly for infinite draw and discard triggers.
With [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Relic of Legends]], [[Pemmin's Aura]] can proliferate infinitely.
[[Crystalline Crawler]] tapped by [[Pemmin's Aura]] combines with [[Steel Overseer]] to pile up counters repeatedly.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it becomes tapped.
Untaps for infinite colorless mana with Zirda.
Cuts activation costs, enables Basalt Monolith loop.
Untaps creatures to chain triggers and proliferate.
Draws and discards whenever tapped repeatedly.
Stations into an extra-turn engine with Scepter.
Grants an extra turn when counters are removed.
Taps legendary creatures for mana, feeds proliferate loop.

assessment.line: The deck leans entirely on artifacts, so a sweeper like [[Vandalblast]] would gut [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]]'s board.
Without [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] on board, proliferate triggers stop and counters grow far slower.
The deck has little combat presence, so a blocker-heavy board can stall its artifact attackers.
Removing [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] before it loops with [[Pemmin's Aura]] stops that draw engine cold.
Many tapped dual lands like [[Mystic Monastery]] can slow starts in a three-color Jeskai base.

reply.overview: This colorless deck ramps hard with artifact mana before casting [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5, turning every big colorless spell into a double cascade off cards like [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] and [[Artisan of Kozilek]]. The engine grinds opponents down through annihilator triggers and repeated removal, while [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] can produce infinite colorless mana to fuel late-game plays.

strategy.text: Ramp through artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Thran Dynamo]] to accelerate toward big spells.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 to turn colorless 7-drops into double cascades.
Chain cascades from cards like [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] and [[Artisan of Kozilek]] for value.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana to close games.
Use annihilator creatures like [[It That Betrays]] to strip opponents' boards while attacking.

keep.text: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] and a path to colorless ramp into bigger spells is strong.
Early mana rocks plus [[Mind Stone]] to keep drawing into the plan is a keep.

sendBack.text: A hand with 0 lands and no way to fix mana should go back.
Five or more lands with no ramp pieces like [[Thran Dynamo]] is too clunky.

tips.text: [[Thought-Knot Seer]] strips a card before [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] cascades reveal your plan to opponents.
[[Basalt Monolith]] untaps for {3} and combines with [[Forsaken Monument]] doubling its colorless output toward infinite mana.
[[Darksteel Monolith]] can let you cast a colorless spell free, then [[Abstruse Archaic]] copies its triggered ability.

keyCards.job: Grants double cascade to big colorless spells
Pairs with Forsaken Monument for colorless mana
Doubles colorless mana and pumps creatures
Refills hand and counters spells via discard
Reanimates a creature when cast, triggers annihilator
Discounts colorless spells and exiles threats
Finds colorless creatures and discounts Eldrazi
Strips a card from opponent's hand on entry

assessment.line: The deck leans heavily on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and has no answer if opponents bring artifact hate.
Losing [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] removes the cascade engine that powers the whole top end.
Removing [[Basalt Monolith]] before it combines with [[Forsaken Monument]] denies the infinite mana line.

reply.overview: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] leads a Naya Dinosaur deck that ramps to a critical mass of big creatures, slams [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] into combat, and cascades Dinosaurs onto the battlefield off its trigger. Enrage creatures like [[Polyraptor]], [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Ripjaw Raptor]] turn incidental damage into value, and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] plus [[Polyraptor]] can go infinite to flood the board and close the game.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Arcane Signet]] and [[Sol Ring]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to hit a player and cheat Dinosaurs straight onto the battlefield.
Trigger Enrage creatures such as [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with fights or damage to snowball the board.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] to create endless Dinosaur tokens and damage.
Close with trample threats like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] and [[Thrasta, Tempest's Roar]] once the board is wide.

keep.text: A hand with early mana and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] to find more Dinosaurs is worth keeping.
Keep a hand that ramps into [[Ranging Raptors]] to fix and expand your lands.

sendBack.text: A hand with no way to reach white or red mana for [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] should go back.
A hand stuck on one color with none of your 9 ramp pieces is too slow to keep.

tips.text: Damage [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to put counters on every other creature, then fight again with [[Zacama, Primal Calamity]].
[[Fight Rigging]] grows a creature each combat; once it reaches power 7 you can cast the hidden card free.
Use [[Boxing Ring]] to fight an entering creature into [[Polyraptor]], triggering Enrage to copy it.

keyCards.job: Combat damage puts Dinosaurs into play free.
Finds Dinosaurs and loops damage with Polyraptor.
Copies itself endlessly when damaged.
Spreads counters across the board when damaged.
Pairs with Bellowing Aegisaur for counter synergy.
Discovers extra Dinosaurs whenever one enters.
Discounts creatures and damages them on entry.
Clears non-Dinosaur creatures when cast from hand.

assessment.line: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and has few ways to answer an opposing enchantment prison.
Only 1 of 7 interaction pieces costs two or less and none are instant speed, so a fast combo like one built around [[Walking Ballista]] can resolve before this deck answers it.
Without connecting with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]], the deck loses its main way to cheat Dinosaurs into play.
The plan relies heavily on combat damage from creatures like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]], so fogs or pillowfort effects can stall it out.
Removing [[Polyraptor]] before it is damaged shuts down the loop with [[Forerunner of the Empire]].

reply.overview: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] leads a mono Red goblin tribal deck that floods the board with tokens and turns them sideways or sacrifices them for damage. With [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] alongside [[Skirk Prospector]], the deck can chain infinite commander casts, infinite hasty goblin tokens, and infinite death triggers, closing the game outright. Even without the combo, repeated taps of [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] backed by haste enablers and sacrifice payoffs like [[Goblin Bombardment]] and [[Pashalik Mons]] grind opponents down.

strategy.text: Ramp early with [[Sol Ring]], [[Mind Stone]], or [[Arcane Signet]] to cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4.
Protect [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and tap it to flood the board with Goblin tokens each turn.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Skirk Prospector]] and [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for infinite casts and tokens.
Grant haste with [[Goblin Warchief]], [[Bloodlust Inciter]], or [[Dragon Breath]] so new tokens attack immediately.
Close with burn like [[Goblin War Strike]] or sacrifice outlets such as [[Goblin Bombardment]] for reach.

keep.text: A hand with early ramp and [[Skirk Prospector]] to fuel later combo turns.
A hand that curves into [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] with a way to protect it.

sendBack.text: A hand with no red sources to support the deck's heavy red costs.
A hand lacking any path to Goblins or token generators like [[Dragon Fodder]].

tips.text: Sacrifice extra Goblins to [[Skirk Prospector]] for mana, then recast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] if it dies.
[[Goblin Bombardment]] turns tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] into direct damage before a board wipe hits.
[[Goblin Warchief]] gives your Goblins haste so tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can attack the turn they arrive.

keyCards.job: Taps to multiply Goblins under your control.
Grants haste and discounts Goblin spells for the combo line.
Alternate haste enabler for the infinite cast line.
Sacrifices Goblins for mana to loop the combo.
Converts dying Goblins into direct damage.
Sacrifice outlet turning tokens into damage.
Finds key Goblin pieces for the engine.
Accelerates toward casting the commander early.

assessment.line: The deck does not rely on recursion, so graveyard hate like [[Rest in Peace]] barely matters.
Key payoffs like [[Goblin Bombardment]] sit undefended if an opponent plays [[Vandalblast]].
Without [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on board, the token flood and the infinite line with [[Skirk Prospector]] stop entirely.
The plan leans on wide combat with tokens, so [[Ghostly Prison]]-style taxes blunt the attack.
Removing [[Skirk Prospector]] before the loop starts denies the infinite line with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].

reply.overview: This Jeskai deck led by [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] turns the attacks and deaths of its many Gods into experience counters, which [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] converts into +1/+1 counters and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] converts into card draw and direct damage. It ramps with pieces like [[Smothering Tithe]] and [[Sol Ring]] into a board of Gods such as [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]], [[The Locust God]], and [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]], then wins by repeated combat damage and incidental burn as those Gods attack and tokens flood the board.

strategy.text: Ramp with [[Sol Ring]], [[Arcane Signet]], and [[Smothering Tithe]] to reach the commanders by around turn 4.
Attack with Gods to trigger [[Kratos, Stoic Father]]'s experience counters, then place +1/+1 counters each end step.
Tap [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to turn experience counters into cards and 2 damage to each opponent.
Deploy [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] and [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] to snowball tokens and chip damage.
Use [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Contentious Plan]] to proliferate counters faster across the board.

keep.text: A hand with [[Smothering Tithe]] and a couple of lands ramps into the plan early.
Early mana plus [[Jeska's Will]] sets up a big turn into the commanders.

sendBack.text: A hand lacking any red or white source struggles to cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] on curve.
A hand with no blue sources can't support [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s activation.

tips.text: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]]'s experience counters feed directly into [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s draw and damage ability.
[[The Locust God]] turns every card drawn into an Insect, and [[Teferi's Ageless Insight]] doubles most of those draws.
[[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] pings opponents whenever [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] creates Rebel tokens on attack.

keyCards.job: Generates experience counters and distributes +1/+1 counters.
Converts experience counters into cards and opponent damage.
Builds Treasure mana off opponents' draws.
Doubles up for huge mana or card advantage with commanders out.
Attacks to make experience counters and Rebel tokens.
Punishes opponents whenever a creature enters.
Turns every draw into a hasty flying Insect token.
Proliferates counters whenever a spell is cast.

assessment.line: Only three of the deck's interaction cards act at instant speed, so a fast combo can resolve before [[Chaos Warp]] answers it.
Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] on board the experience engine stalls and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] has nothing to convert.
The plan leans on combat damage from Gods, so a fog like [[Ghostly Prison]] on the other side of the table slows it down.
Several tapped duals and three-color demands mean [[Ojer Pakpatiq, Deepest Epoch // Temple of Cyclical Time]] and friends can come online slowly.

reply.overview: This mono-Blue wizard-tribal deck led by [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] taxes down and chains instants and sorceries while a wall of counterspells protects its engine. Wins come from looping draws with [[Psychosis Crawler]] or [[Triskaidekaphile]], or by assembling the infinite loop of [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] or [[Ghostly Flicker]] for repeated death, ETB, and magecraft triggers that grind opponents out.

strategy.text: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 to cheapen every instant and sorcery that follows.
Chain cheap draw spells like [[Preordain]] and [[Ponder]] to dig for counterspells and combo pieces.
Hold up [[Wizard's Retort]] and [[Mana Leak]] to protect your board and stall opponents.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite copied triggers that close the game.
If that's unavailable, loop [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] for the same infinite ETB engine.

keep.text: A hand with early ramp and a path toward [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] is worth keeping.
Keeping lands plus [[Preordain]] to dig toward [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] is solid.

sendBack.text: A hand with no early plays and nothing to protect your tempo should go back.
Too many expensive spells and no cheap interaction like [[Negate]] is a mulligan.

tips.text: Cast [[Sublime Epiphany]] targeting itself with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] on the stack to generate an infinite loop of triggers.
Use [[Ghostly Flicker]] to flicker [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] alongside an artifact for repeated ETB triggers.
Cast instants through [[Archmage of Runes]] to reduce their cost and draw a card off each one.

keyCards.job: Copies spells to enable the infinite loop
Counters, bounces, and copies itself in the loop
Flickers Naru Meha for repeated triggers
Reduces costs and draws cards off counters
Cheapens spells and draws on every cast
Turns extra draws into damage output
Wins by holding exactly thirteen cards

assessment.line: The deck has no way to answer an opposing artifact or enchantment like a hypothetical [[Null Rod]].
Losing [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] slows the cost reduction engine but the deck still draws cards without it.
Removing [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] at its enter trigger stops the infinite loop with [[Sublime Epiphany]].

reply.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninjutsu deck where cheap unblockable creatures slip in, swap for ninjas, and trigger damage off revealed cards' mana value, draining opponents while drawing cards and finding more ninjas.

strategy.text: Play an early unblockable body like [[Slither Blade]] or [[Tormented Soul]] to enable ninjutsu.
Cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] around turn 3 and hold her for ninjutsu swaps.
Bounce the attacker to ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or other ninjas for card advantage and damage.
Use [[Higure, the Still Wind]] to tutor more ninjas once combat damage connects.
Refill with [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] and [[Moon-Circuit Hacker]] triggers to keep attacking.

keep.text: An unblockable creature alongside [[Mistblade Shinobi]] sets up an early ninjutsu swap.
Lands backed by [[Dimir Signet]] smooth early plays toward turn 3 [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].

sendBack.text: A hand heavy on black sources with no blue leaves ninjutsu costs uncastable.
Too many spells and no early unblockable creature stalls the whole plan.

tips.text: Bounce [[Mist-Syndicate Naga]] with ninjutsu to copy it, then use the copy to ninjutsu in [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] later.
[[Satoru Umezawa]] gives creatures in hand ninjutsu, letting [[Fallen Shinobi]] enter from a Satoru-granted ninjutsu swap.
[[Silver-Fur Master]] reduces ninjutsu costs and pumps other ninjas like [[Nashi, Moon Sage's Scion]] once it attacks.

keyCards.job: Turns revealed cards into opponent life loss
Grants hand creatures ninjutsu and draws extra cards
Finds more Ninja creatures after connecting
Steals a creature from an opponent's graveyard

Cuts ninjutsu costs and pumps other ninjas
Creates Treasure tokens off ninja damage

assessment.line: The deck has no way to answer an opposing artifact like a hypothetical [[Null Rod]] stopping [[Sol Ring]].
Without [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on board the life-loss trigger stops and ninjutsu swaps lose their payoff.
The plan depends entirely on unblocked combat damage, so a pillowfort like [[Ghostly Prison]] could slow every attacker.
